1. This is an appeal under Section 374(3)(A) Cr.P.C. challenging the judgment of conviction dated 17.10.2022 and order on the point of sentence dated 20.10.2022 passed by Ms. Nabeela Wali, Ld.
Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Kiran by Kiran Gupta Gupta 15:15:51 +0530 New Delhi.
The Ld. ACCM vide impugned judgment dated 17.10.2022 had convicted the appellant for violation of offence punishable under Section 2(ia) r/w Rule 44(c) r/w S. 7 of PFA punishable under S.
16(1)(a) of Prevention of Food Adulteration (hereinafter referred as PFA) Act and violation of S. 14A of the Act punishable under S. 16(1)(c) of the Act. Vide order dated 20.10.2022, the Ld. ACMM has sentenced the appellant to undergo SI for six months alongwith fine of Rs. 1,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 16(1)(a) of the Act. Further the appellant has been sentenced to SI for period already undergone and fine of Rs. 500/- for offence punishable u/s 16(1)(c) of the Act. 
Benefit u/s 428 Cr.P.C. also given to the appellant. 
2. Heard Arguments on the present appeal and perused the appeal file as well as trial court record.
3. The brief facts of the present case are that on 20.06.2019, at about 02:45 pm, Food Inspector (FI)
Sanjeev Kumar Gupta and Sh. Mittar Pal under the supervision of Local Health Authority (LHA)/SDM Sh. R.K. Sharma visited the Kiran byDate:Kiran Gupta Gupta 2024.07.03 15:15:57 +0530 premises of M/s Baniya General Store, Shop No. 315, Main Bazaar, Subzi Mandi,
Delhi-110007 where the appellants were found conducting business of various food articles including 'ghee', which were lying stored for sale for human consumption in open aluminum tub bearing no label declaration. The sample was seized as per rules. Each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked, sealed and necessary documents including Notice as per Form-VI alongwith Panchnama etc. was prepared at the spot. Thereafter, one counterpart of sample was sent to Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA. That vide report dated 06.07.2009, the PA found the sample to be substandard not confirming to the standards on the grounds that the BR reading exceeded the prescribed maximum Ravi Kumar vs Delhi Administration on 3 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153473047/
2 limit of 43 and the Reichert value was less than the prescribed minimum limit of 28. It also gave a positive B.T. test which should be negative in ghee. Subsequently, on the basis of the report, the present complaint was filed against the appellant and his father Sh. Raj Kumar. During trial, Sh. Raj Kumar expired and proceedings against him were abated vide order dated 30.01.2020. 
 Digitally  signed by  Kiran Kiran Gupta  Date:
 Gupta 2024.07.03  15:16:02  +0530 4. Since the complaint was filed by a public servant in writing, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the appellant alongwith his father was summoned vide order dated 23.11.2019. After recording, pre-charge evidence, vide order dated 12.05.2010 charge u/s 16(1)(a)
and 16(1)(c) r/w Section 7 of PFA Act was framed against the appellant to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 
5. The prosecution examined three witnesses in support of its case. PW-1 is FI Sanjeev Kumar Gupta, he in his testimony exhibited the documents Ex.PW1/A to Ex.PW1/L and Mark X. PW-2 is Sh. R.K. Sharma (SDM/LHA). He deposed on similar lines as PW1 and identified his signatures on relevant documents. PW-3 Sh. Mittar Pal, Retd. FA, deposed that on the request of PW1 he joined the sample proceedings. He relied upon the pamphlet Ex.PW1/A1 and his signatures on Ex.PW1/D1. 
All these witnesses were duly cross-examined. 
6. The statement of appellant was recorded under Digitally signed by Kiran Kiran Gupta Date:
Gupta 2024.07.03 15:16:08 +0530 section 313 Cr.P.C. on 09.12.2013 wherein he denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. He stated that the present complaint was filed because his father / co-accused had given complaint against nearby shopkeepers who were indulging in food adulteration. He in his defence, examined himself as DW3 and two witnesses - DW-1 Sh. Rajesh & DW-2 Sh. Laxmi Narain. 
These witnesses were duly cross examined by ld. SPP. 
GROUNDS OF APPEAL Ravi Kumar vs Delhi Administration on 3 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153473047/
3 7. The appellant has taken the following grounds of appeal. 
a. That the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that the respondent has not complied with mandatory procedures and rules under the Act. 
b. That the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that appellants right to seek second opinion from CFL under S. 13(2) of PFA was violated by the respondent as no PA report was ever received by the appellant. The respondent further failed to prove that the appellant was duly served with the PA report via post. 
 Kiran by Kiran Gupta  Gupta 15:16:19  +0530  c. That the Trial Court failed to appreciate that there was inordinate delay in instituting prosecution in the present case. The PA report was received on 06.07.2009 by the respondent and prosecution was instituted much lateron 23.11.2009. 
d. That the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that no independent witness was joined by the respondent while purchasing samples.
e. That the Ld. Trial Court did not appreciate the material contradiction in the testimony of witnesses examined by the respondent. 
It is prayed that in view of grounds of appeal, the impugned judgment dated 17.10.2022 and order on the point of sentence dated 20.10.2022 may kindly be set aside. 
ANALYSIS AND FINDINGS 8. Heard Ld. Counsel for appellant and Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor for Department and perused the appeal file as Digitally signed by Kiran Kiran Gupta Date:
 Gupta 2024.07.03  15:16:26  +0530 Ravi Kumar vs Delhi Administration on 3 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153473047/
4 well as trial court record. The Ld. Counsel for the appellant has stated that the Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate that the witnesses deposed before the court were against the facts and contradictory to each other. Though the appellant has taken the said ground, however, he has nowhere described as to how and in which manner the deposition of witnesses were against the facts or contrary to each other. No contradiction in the deposition of witnesses which is fatal to the case of prosecution, is pointed out by the appellant. In fact, the Ld. ACMM in para 20 of the judgment has discussed the contradictions which were argued by ld. Counsel for appellant before her and rightly held that the said contradictions do not constitute material contradictions and are formal in nature. 
As regards the plea of non joining of the public witnesses is concerned, it is also not fatal to the case of prosecution in the present case. 
9. Though the appellant has contended that the Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate that the respondent has not complied with the mandatory procedures and rules under the Digitally signed by Kiran Kiran Gupta Date:
 Gupta 2024.07.03  15:16:32  +0530 Act, however, he has failed to point out any such Rule or violation of the procedure by the respondent. At one point, the appellant has pleaded that he had not received the PA report and on the other hand he had taken the plea that the prosecution was instituted much later on 23.11.2009,
while he received the PA report on 06.07.2009. Even otherwise also, respondent has duly proved the service of the PA report Ex.PW1/G through postal receipts Ex.PW1/K and Ex.PW1/L.
10. Now coming to the contention of appellant that the ld. ACMM has wrongly placed reliance on the PA report and his right to seek second opinion from CFL under 13(2) PFA was violated. It is settled law that the accused has the right for getting the sample analyzed through CFL by moving appropriate application within the limitation period. In the present case, the appellant did not exercise such right. On the contrary, PW-1 proved the postal receipt Ex.PW1/L and Ex.PW1/K.
Ravi Kumar vs Delhi Administration on 3 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153473047/
5 Further, as per the report Ex.PW1/G, BR reading exceeded the prescribed maximum limit and the RM value was less than the prescribed minimum limit. The BT Test (Baudouin Test) was positive. 
The Digitally signed by Kiran Kiran Gupta Date:
 Gupta 2024.07.03  15:16:43  +0530 appellant has failed to tender any explanation as to how the BR reading went so high in case of ghee sold by him. The appellant has failed to point out any flaw in the findings of Ld. ACMM in placing reliance upon the PA report. As regards the delay of few months in sending the sample to RFL is concerned, the ld. ACMM has dealt with the said aspect in para 30 of the judgment. 
11. The Ld. Trial Court vide detailed judgment has given clear findings with regard to all the defences taken by the appellants. There is no illegality or infirmity in the impugned judgment of conviction dated 17.10.2022. The judgment dated 17.10.2022 passed by Ld. ACMM, New Delhi,
Patiala House Courts in CC no. 1996/09 (42902/16) is upheld. Accordingly, the appeal against the judgment dated 17.10.2022 is dismissed. 
ORDER ON SENTENCE 12. The appellant in the present appeal has also challenged the order on the point of sentence dated 20.10.2022. It is argued that the PFA act has been recently amended which Digitally signed by Kiran Kiran Gupta Date:
 Gupta 2024.07.03  15:16:49  +0530 Ravi Kumar vs Delhi Administration on 3 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153473047/
6 prescribes the punishment of fine also. It is prayed that in view of pendency of case for a long period, a lenient view may kindly be taken. On the other hand it is argued on behalf of department by Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor that the Ld. Trial Court has already taken a lenient view and there is no illegality in the order of sentence. 
13. The appellant/convict is convicted for commission of offence punishable under Section 16(1)(a)
& 16(1)(c) of PFA Act. Under S. 16(1)(a) minimum sentence of imprisonment is given. However,
w.e.f. 15.10.2007, new Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 came into force in which, for similar offence, the punishment of only fine has been prescribed. 
14. In view of above, question for consideration before this court is whether after repeal of earlier Act and introduction of new Act which contains the lesser punishment, the court can take a lenient view of awarding the lesser punishment. On this issue, Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as M/s A. K. Sarkar & Company & Anr. Vs. The State of Digitally signed by Kiran Kiran Gupta Date:
 Gupta 2024.07.03  15:16:55  +0530 West Bengal & Ors, Special Leave Petition(Criminal) No.6095 of 2018, dated 07.03.2024, has observed that:
"Whether the appellant can be granted the benefit of the new legislation and be awarded a lesser punishment as is presently prescribed under the new law. This court in T. Barai VS. Henry Ah Hoe (1983) 1 SCC 177, had held that when an amendment is beneficial to the accused it can be applied even to cases pending the courts where such a provision did not exist at the time of commission of offence." 
15. The recent judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case M/s A. K. Sarkar & Company & Anr.
(Supra) has made it clear that if there is an amendment in the Act, which is beneficial to the accused,
it can be applied even to the pending cases in the court where such provision was not in existence. 
The ratio of judgment M/s A. K. Sarkar & Company & Anr. (Supra) is squarely applicable to the facts of present case. Therefore on the basis of above case law, I have no hesitation to hold that this court can take a lenient view as per new provisions of law. 
 Digitally  signed by Ravi Kumar vs Delhi Administration on 3 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153473047/
7  Kiran Kiran Gupta  Date:
 Gupta 2024.07.03  15:17:02  +0530 16. In the present case the complaint was filed on 23.11.2009. The appellant was held guilty and convicted for the offences punishable under Section 16(1)(a) & 16(1)(c) r/w S. 7 of PFA Act for selling adulterated food and has been sentenced as follows:
a. The appellant has been sentenced to undergo SI for six months alongwith fine of Rs. 1,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 16(1)(a) of the Act. 
b. The appellant has been sentenced to SI for period already undergone and fine of Rs. 500/- for offence punishable u/s 16(1)(c) of the Act. 
17. The appellant has already faced the trauma of trial for almost 15 years. The circumstances disclosed by Ld. Counsel for the appellant/convict also warrants taking of a lenient view. 
Considering all the aspects; nature of offence as alleged, submissions made, a lenient view is taken and the sentence imposed by the Ld. Trial court vide order dated 20.10.2022 for commission of offence under Section 16(1)(a) of PFA Act is Digitally signed by Kiran Kiran Date:
Gupta Gupta 15:17:14 2024.07.03 +0530 modified qua the appellant. The appellant is sentenced to pay only fine of Rs. 50,000/-. The order on sentence for the offence under S. 16(1)(c) is upheld. 
18. The fine amount shall be deposited by the appellant before the concerned court within a period of 15 days from today. In case of default of payment of fine, the appellant shall undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 60 days. 
Appeal is accordingly partly allowed. 
Attested copy of the judgment be given to the appellant/convict, free of cost. Trial court record be sent back to the court concerned alongwith copy of this judgment. 
Ravi Kumar vs Delhi Administration on 3 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153473047/
8 Appeal file be consigned to record room after necessary compliance. 
 Digitally  signed by  Kiran Kiran Gupta  Date:

 NEW DELHI DISTRICT,

summary.facts:
The Ld. ACCM vide impugned judgment dated 17.10.2022 had convicted the appellant for violation of offence punishable under Section 2(ia) r/w Rule 44(c) r/w S. 7 of PFA punishable under S.
16(1)(a) of Prevention of Food Adulteration (hereinafter referred as PFA) Act and violation of S. 14A of the Act punishable under S. 16(1)(c) of the Act.

a. That the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that the respondent has not complied with mandatory procedures and rules under the Act.
b. That the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that appellants right to seek second opinion from CFL under S. 13(2) of PFA was violated by the respondent as no PA report was ever received by the appellant.
The respondent further failed to prove that the appellant was duly served with the PA report via post.
That the Trial Court failed to appreciate that there was inordinate delay in instituting prosecution in the present case.
The PA report was received on 06.07.2009 by the respondent and prosecution was instituted much lateron 23.11.2009.

d. That the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that no independent witness was joined by the respondent while purchasing samples.
e. That the Ld. Trial Court did not appreciate the material contradiction in the testimony of witnesses examined by the respondent.
summary.arguments: Though the appellant has taken the said ground, however, he has nowhere described as to how and in which manner the deposition of witnesses were against the facts or contrary to each other.
summary.ANALYSIS:
No contradiction in the deposition of witnesses which is fatal to the case of prosecution, is pointed out by the appellant.

As regards the plea of non joining of the public witnesses is concerned, it is also not fatal to the case of prosecution in the present case.
It is settled law that the accused has the right for getting the sample analyzed through CFL by moving appropriate application within the limitation period.
In the present case, the appellant did not exercise such right.
On the contrary, PW-1 proved the postal receipt Ex.PW1/L and Ex.PW1/K.
